territorial_scope.description: Applies to the PW Digital Gateway study area along Pageland Lane in Prince William County, Virginia, and to three named rezoning applications within it.

evidence.provision: Adoption notice (Board of County Supervisors Res. No. 22-508)
evidence.quote: On November 1, 2022, the Prince William Board of County Supervisors adopted Comprehensive Plan Amendment #CPA2021-00004 PW Digital Gateway.

summary.short: Prince William County Board of Supervisors adopted Comprehensive Plan Amendment CPA2021-00004 (PW Digital Gateway) on 1 November 2022, creating a technology corridor along Pageland Lane for data center uses. Board rezoning approvals for the area were later declared void by court order, while the plan amendment remains in place.
summary.long: Prince William County's Board of County Supervisors initiated Comprehensive Plan Amendment CPA2021-00004 on 20 July 2021 (Res. No. 21-445) and adopted it on 1 November 2022 (Res. No. 22-508). The amendment, described as a request to create a technology corridor along Pageland Lane for data center uses that would use existing transmission and fiber optic infrastructure, initially proposed changing Long Range Land Use from AE and ER to Technology/Flex with a T-3 transect. The study area was expanded to 194 parcels and 2,139 acres between Route 234 and Route 29. Three rezoning applications for the area (REZ2022-00032, REZ2022-00033, REZ2022-00036) carry proffers dated December 2023. A Court of Appeals decision of 31 March 2026 was stayed; by order of 29 July 2026 the Board's rezoning approvals were declared void and zoning reverts to the district in place before approval. The Comprehensive Plan Amendment remains in place. Any future rezoning must follow the normal application process, with Planning Commission and Board public hearings. The page also lists related data center overlay review materials and process tasks. The source is a county project webpage summarizing the process, not the adopted plan text.

notes: The source is a county web page (update of August 5, 2026), not the court orders, the adopting resolutions or the proffers. The July 29, 2026 order and March 31, 2026 decision are described, not quoted. The registry's 'approved 2023-12-13', 'Circuit Court 2025' and 'repealed' are not stated in the text; the text says the rezoning decisions are void and gives proffer dates of December 10 and 11, 2023. Internal inconsistencies: the page says the section on the adopted CPA 'will not be updated' yet still shows tasks as ongoing and the November 1, 2022 hearing as future; the project overview says the original corridor had 27 parcels, while the expanded study area is later given as 194 parcels and 2,139 acres. The update says the CPA 'remains in place' while the rezonings are void.

thresholds.note: The page describes a Comprehensive Plan Amendment and rezonings but states no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The study-area figures (194 parcels, 2,139 acres) and the 250,000 sq ft data center in the fiscal analysis description are descriptive, not legal thresholds.

definitions.note: The page defines no scope-determining terms. It refers to data centers only as uses on the Board's List of Targeted Industries, which is not a definition.

obligations.note: The document is an informational county web page (PW Digital Gateway) that reports a court order and staff steps. It contains no operative provisions such as articles or sections imposing duties. Its statements about staff compliance and property reassessment describe consequences of court orders that are not reproduced in the document, so none is coded as an obligation.

enforcement.note: No sanction regime is stated in the document. The only reference is that each property 'will need to be reviewed to take into consideration any applicable penalties and interest' after the zoning reassessment; the text does not identify the penalty, its authority, its trigger or its amount, so no entry is coded.
